subject: mountain valley town
title: What If Your Town Got No Sunlight for Six Months? One Put Mirrors on a Mountain

scenes.text: What if your town got no sunlight for six months? One waited a century for the fix.
A town of 3,500 people in Norway sits at the bottom of a steep valley.
From late September to mid-March, the mountains block every direct ray.
In 1913 its founder proposed giant mirrors on the mountain. The technology wasn't there, so he built a cable car up to the sunlight.
A hundred years later, in 2013, three mirrors went up. Each is 17 square meters, steered by computer to follow the Sun.
They throw a patch of sunlight about 600 square meters onto the town square. In winter, people gather to stand in it.

description:
What if your town got no direct sunlight for half the year? Rjukan, a Norwegian town of about 3,500 people, sits in a valley so steep that the mountains block the Sun from late September to mid-March.
Its founder suggested mirrors in 1913 but built a cable car to the sunlight instead. In 2013 the town finally installed three computer-steered mirrors of 17 square metres each on the mountainside; they reflect a patch of sunlight of about 600 square metres onto the town square. The project cost about five million Norwegian kroner.
